example_sentence: Governments must act now to mitigate the effects of climate change.
collocations: mitigate the effects; mitigate the impact; mitigate risk
root_analysis: mit-(緩和、變柔軟) + -igate(使…) → 使變柔和

example_sentence: There has been a substantial increase in tuition fees over the past decade.
collocations: a substantial increase; substantial evidence; a substantial amount of
root_analysis: sub-(在下) + stant(站立, 同 stand) + -ial → 站得住腳的 → 有實質分量的
notes: 寫作 Task 2 講程度時的高分替換字

example_sentence: Researchers conducted a survey of two thousand university students.
collocations: conduct research; conduct a survey; conduct an experiment
root_analysis: con-(一起) + duct(引導, 同 conduct 電導) → 引導著進行

example_sentence: Migrant workers constitute nearly a third of the city's workforce.
collocations: constitute a threat; constitute a majority; constitute evidence
root_analysis: con-(一起) + stitut(建立, 同 institute) → 一起建立成 → 組成
synonyms: make up; form; comprise; account for

example_sentence: The spread of misinformation undermines public trust in journalism.
collocations: undermine confidence; undermine authority; undermine efforts
root_analysis: under-(下面) + mine(挖礦) → 在底下挖 → 動搖根基

example_sentence: Many educators advocate replacing final exams with continuous assessment.
collocations: advocate a policy; advocate for reform; strongly advocate
root_analysis: ad-(朝向) + voc(聲音, 同 voice/vocal) + -ate → 為某事發聲

example_sentence: The council allocates a fixed budget to each district every year.
collocations: allocate resources; allocate funding; allocate time
root_analysis: ad-(朝向) + loc(地方, 同 location) + -ate → 放到該去的位置

example_sentence: The government implemented stricter penalties for repeat offenders.
collocations: implement a policy; implement measures; implement reforms
root_analysis: im-(進入) + ple(填滿, 同 complete) + -ment → 填滿內容 → 付諸實行
synonyms: carry out; enforce; put into practice; execute

example_sentence: Cities need sustainable transport systems that do not rely on private cars.
collocations: sustainable development; sustainable growth; environmentally sustainable
root_analysis: sus-(在下) + tain(持有, 同 contain/retain) + -able → 在底下撐得住的

example_sentence: Toxins from processed food gradually accumulate in the body.
collocations: accumulate wealth; accumulate evidence; accumulate over time
root_analysis: ac-(朝向) + cumul(堆積, 同 cumulative) + -ate → 一層層堆起來
synonyms: build up; amass; gather; pile up

example_sentence: Air quality in the capital has deteriorated sharply since 2010.
collocations: deteriorate rapidly; conditions deteriorate; deteriorating health
root_analysis: deterior-(更壞, 拉丁文 deterior) + -ate → 變得更壞
notes: Task 1 描述下降趨勢也可用

example_sentence: Longer holidays do not compensate for consistently low wages.
collocations: compensate for; compensate workers; adequately compensate
root_analysis: com-(一起) + pens(秤重、支付, 同 expense/pension) + -ate → 秤平、補足
synonyms: make up for; offset; reimburse; counterbalance

example_sentence: Analysts attribute the drop in sales to the rise of online shopping.
collocations: attribute the rise to; be attributed to; widely attributed
root_analysis: at-(朝向) + tribut(給予, 同 tribute/contribute) → 把功勞或原因歸給…
notes: attribute A to B 的搭配一定要記

example_sentence: Budget constraints forced the hospital to postpone the new wing.
collocations: financial constraints; time constraints; impose constraints
root_analysis: con-(一起) + strain/strict(拉緊, 同 restrict) → 綁緊 → 限制

example_sentence: Rapid urbanisation makes some loss of farmland inevitable.
collocations: an inevitable consequence; an inevitable decline; almost inevitable
root_analysis: in-(不) + evit(避開, 同 evade) + -able → 無法避開的
synonyms: unavoidable; inescapable; certain; bound to happen

example_sentence: Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to coastal communities.
collocations: pose a threat; pose a risk; pose a challenge; pose a question
root_analysis: pos-(放置, 同 position/expose) → 把某物放到眼前 → 造成、提出
notes: pose a threat 是雅思閱讀高頻搭配

example_sentence: Financial literacy should be part of the national curriculum.
collocations: the school curriculum; curriculum design; a core curriculum
root_analysis: curr-(跑, 同 current/occur) + -iculum → 要跑完的路程 → 課程

example_sentence: Critics argue that mass surveillance erodes personal privacy.
collocations: CCTV surveillance; under surveillance; mass surveillance
root_analysis: sur-(在上面) + veill(看守, 同 vigil 警醒) + -ance → 在上面盯著看

example_sentence: Congestion charges have cut traffic in the city centre by a fifth.
collocations: traffic congestion; ease congestion; severe congestion
root_analysis: con-(一起) + gest(攜帶, 同 digest/gesture) + -ion → 全擠在一起

example_sentence: Childhood obesity has doubled in urban areas over the past twenty years.
collocations: childhood obesity; obesity rates; tackle obesity
root_analysis: obes-(吃過頭而肥, 拉丁 obesus) + -ity → 肥胖的狀態

example_sentence: Denmark now generates over half its electricity from renewable sources.
collocations: renewable energy; renewable sources; shift to renewables
root_analysis: re-(再) + new(新) + -able → 可以一再變新的

example_sentence: Heavier fines act as a deterrent to dangerous driving.
collocations: act as a deterrent; an effective deterrent; a strong deterrent
root_analysis: de-(離開) + terr(恐懼, 同 terror/terrify) + -ent → 使人因害怕而退開

example_sentence: Readers should be aware of the political bias of the newspapers they follow.
collocations: media bias; political bias; a bias towards; unconscious bias
root_analysis: bias 原指保齡球偏一邊滾的斜度 → 偏向某一邊

example_sentence: Between 2005 and 2010, sales fluctuated between 20 and 35 million units.
collocations: fluctuate wildly; fluctuate between; figures fluctuated
root_analysis: flu(流動, 同 fluid/influence) + -ate → 像水一樣起起伏伏
synonyms: vary; oscillate; swing; go up and down
notes: Task 1 描述不規則變化的首選字

example_sentence: After a sharp rise, the figure plateaued at around 60 per cent.
collocations: reach a plateau; plateau at; plateau after
root_analysis: 法文 plat(平的, 同 plate/plain) → 高原 → 走平的階段
synonyms: level off; stabilise; flatten out; remain steady

example_sentence: Unemployment peaked at 12 per cent in 2009 before falling steadily.
collocations: peak at; reach a peak; a peak of; peak in 2009
root_analysis: peak 山頂 → 最高點；peak at + 數值 是固定用法
synonyms: reach a maximum; culminate; top out; hit a high
notes: 注意 peak at 數值 / peak in 年份

example_sentence: Spending on housing and transport rose to 30 and 18 per cent respectively.
collocations: A and B respectively; rose to X and Y respectively
root_analysis: re-(回) + spect(看, 同 inspect/respect) + -ive-ly → 各自回頭對應著看
notes: 放句尾，讓兩組數據一次講完

example_sentence: Long working hours take a heavy toll on people's mental health.
collocations: take its toll on; take a heavy toll; take a toll on health
root_analysis: toll 原指過路費 → 走這條路要付的代價 → 造成損耗
synonyms: damage; wear down; have a negative effect on; harm
notes: Part 3 講負面影響時很自然

example_sentence: Online courses can help bridge the gap between rural and urban students.
collocations: bridge the gap between; help bridge the gap; bridge the digital gap
root_analysis: bridge(橋) 當動詞 → 在落差上架橋 → 弭平差距
synonyms: close the gap; narrow the divide; reconcile

example_sentence: Social media is a double-edged sword: it connects people but also spreads rumours.
collocations: prove to be a double-edged sword; a double-edged sword for; cut both ways
root_analysis: double-edged 雙刃 → 兩邊都會割到 → 有利也有弊
synonyms: a mixed blessing; a trade-off; cut both ways
notes: Part 3 討論利弊的萬用開場
